result.decision_rationale:
All 53 focused tests passed on the candidate. R2-F3 remains open because the evaluator can characterize a survivor stop inside the declared zero-stop window. It can also characterize a callback observed too late to enter the terminal list and a successful stop paired with zero attempts.

## Continuation for Claude

Use the collector’s recording order to reconcile selection, retirement, sampling and disposal. The loop deadline gives a lower bound on the terminal read. A later recorded disposal stop gives an upper bound on callbacks already copied into the terminal list. Preserve the valid callback between the last periodic sample and the terminal read. Reconcile stop counts with the request fields for the same posting, require readable posting identities and timestamps, and identify the current reader in each retained-row result.

Exercise the findings on the persisted 224949Z row and its in-memory counterpart through the same entry point. Preserve the two Round6 collector contracts and their historical verdicts. Run the applicable focused gates on the correction commit and carry their wall time into the shared ledger. C1 remains implementation/domain-only. The combined native check belongs to C3.

Four controller receipts at d71bdf2e6071454dc59d54c8eafd64db03172c29 record production compilation, unchanged worktrees and zero failures. The filters were sprint7-visual (22 tests, 2.8 s), summon-playtest-r6 (11, 2.1 s), sprint22- (11, 2.9 s) and native-profile (9, 2.2 s).

Confirmed that impact-cue-playback-verdicts is one of the 22 registered sprint7-visual cases. Its passing assertions cover the original row, both null representations, the six reported regression cases and the retained Round6 outcomes.
Recounted the 11 entries in the frozen parent gate extract. They total 118 selected executions and 19.1 s inside receipts. The extract records 40.1 s batch wall time.
A read-only .NET DateTime.Parse check using invariant culture and RoundtripKind converted the time-only input 23:59:00 to 2026-11-26T04:59:00.0000000Z on the review machine.
inspected: AGENTS.md, docs/VALIDATION-POLICY.md, docs/AGENT-REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md, the mission, OWNER AMENDMENT 1, the developer report and the prior findings ledger.
The full feature diff and the correction since e4c9ed9c5e, including Sprint7ObserverPolicy, S7CallbackLoss, SummonCastCueLifecycle, the cue producer, the domain tests and their registration.
The 224949Z and 223809Z Round7 records, the 202648Z and 200320Z Round6 records, the historical collector implementations, the recovery manifest, the Sprint 7 record and planning row.
limitations: The controller withheld the mixed foreground transcript and supplied candidate-bound gate receipts. The reported 19.1 s local run and 19.7 s controller batch wall time come from the developer’s ledger and report. The four receipt durations independently total 10.0 s.

The new counterexamples below were traced through candidate source and retained observations. The reviewer did not execute the candidate evaluator. The isolated date-parsing check exercised the framework parser only.
C1 produced no recovery package, harness or game session. Runtime restoration is inapplicable. The native 224949Z FAIL belongs to historical candidate 3.

source_inspection_only: Traced the collector’s loop exit, zero-stop read, terminal callback-list copy and subsequent survivor disposal to establish the timing bounds in R2-F3 and R3-F1.
Compared Retire’s write order with the evaluator’s count and lifecycle checks. Inspected the positive-inventory scan, timestamp reader and both reinterpretation output statements.

findings.actual: Line 416 compares the stop only with the last sample at 22:52:08.2900069Z. The collector exits its 12-second loop at or after 22:52:08.4293166Z and only then reads survivorStopAttemptsThroughWindow as zero. A stop at 22:52:08.3500000Z clears the evaluator’s check and the row characterizes.
findings.blocking_rationale: The reader still credits the survivor’s disposal with a stop that the collector’s later zero count rules out.
findings.expected: A stop strictly inside the declared window must conflict with the zero through-window count, including the interval after the last periodic sample.
findings.requested_correction: Use the Round7 retirement time and declared duration as a proven lower bound on the zero-count read. Preserve the distinction between that bound and the unknown exact terminal-read time.
findings.requested_evidence: On both 224949Z representations, refuse a disposal stop at 22:52:08.3500000Z, retain the actual disposal stop at 22:52:08.4634895Z, and continue accepting a withheld callback at 22:52:08.3500000Z with zero periodic counts.
findings.title: Protect the interval between the last sample and the window deadline
findings.trigger: On a 224949Z copy, change only survivorAfterDisposal.cue.stopRequestedUtc to 2026-11-24T22:52:08.3500000Z.

findings.actual: Both callback controls characterize. The lower bound at line 355 uses only the survivor’s posting time. The terminal comparison at line 388 permits any later timestamp when the sample counts are zero. S7CallbackLoss arms the target only after both cues are selected, and copies the terminal list before starting survivor disposal. The same missing order check lets otherRetiredUtc move to 22:51:56.0000000Z, before cue 622 was posted, while its stop still falls within RetiredByOwnId’s one-second tolerance.
findings.blocking_rationale: The evaluator can credit the intervention with a callback it could never have withheld, or credit a retirement that predates the selected cue.
findings.expected: A Round7 withheld callback must be possible after the target was armed and before the terminal list was copied. Both selected cues must already exist when the other source is retired.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the bounds established by each collector’s actual ordering, including posting before retirement and terminal callback capture before a recorded disposal stop. Preserve Round6First’s earlier target assignment. Align the contract comment with the sample producer, which queries survivor playback before stamping utc and reads the callback count afterward.
findings.requested_evidence: Reject the pre-arming callback, post-disposal callback and pre-posting retirement on both 224949Z shapes. Retain the valid late-callback control and the original Round6 dispositions.
findings.title: Bound callback attribution by target selection and survivor disposal
findings.trigger: On separate 224949Z copies, set all sample counts to zero and the sole terminal callback to 22:52:08.5000000Z, after the disposal stop at 08.4634895Z. Alternatively, set all counts to one and the callback to 22:51:55.0000000Z, before other cue 622 was posted at 56.4143168Z.

findings.actual: Both controls characterize. The disposal count comparison can never fail on the acceptance path because windowStops is zero and Count already requires a nonnegative value. At the retirement frame, Advances accepts a stop result that matches the later settled result without reconciling it with the zero attempts read immediately after the cue.
findings.blocking_rationale: A successful request and a subsequent zero count for the same posting are incompatible. Accepting them defeats the required stop-attempt attribution.
findings.expected: SummonCastCueLifecycle.Retire increments StopAttempts before recording a stop result or request time. A count read after those fields must reflect the attempt.
findings.requested_correction: Reconcile each consumed stop result and request time with the attempt count according to that collector’s read order. Account for the producer’s failed-call case, which records an attempt and failure result without a successful request timestamp.
findings.requested_evidence: On both 224949Z shapes, refuse a successful disposal request with zero attempts and an already recorded retirement-frame stop result followed by zero attempts. Keep the original successful disposal control.
findings.title: Reconcile the stop request with the count for the same cue
findings.trigger: Set only survivorAfterDisposal.stopAttempts to zero while retaining its successful stop result and timestamp. Independently, set afterOtherRetired.other.stopResult to stop-requested while retaining otherStopAttempts equal to zero.

findings.actual: Utc uses DateTime.TryParse with RoundtripKind. A time-only value acquires the replay machine’s current date and local offset. On this machine the resulting instant falls after the recorded window and clears the disposal-time check.
findings.blocking_rationale: A fixed evidence row can acquire a different stop date on another day or machine. The inferred date supplies the evidence needed for characterization.
findings.expected: A timestamp with no recorded date cannot establish that the stop occurred after the observation window.
findings.requested_correction: Accept complete collector timestamps and their reparsed date values. Return an unreadable observation when resolving the instant would require supplying missing date or zone information from the replay machine.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise the time-only stop value on both row representations alongside the original round-trip UTC string and parsed date controls.
findings.title: Require a recorded date for lifecycle timestamps

findings.actual: SourceRecord skips a different positive ID before checking its posting fields. For a selected record, Posting accepts an empty event because Text returns a non-null string. Both controls characterize, although PlayImpact itself refuses an empty event name.
findings.blocking_rationale: OWNER AMENDMENT 1 requires a recorded immutable posting identity and limits the failed-post exception to known ID-zero attempts. A bare positive ID or an empty selected event does not establish the required posting.
findings.expected: Positive source records used as inventory evidence must identify a posting. The selected event must have a name.
findings.requested_correction: Validate the immutable posting fields of nonzero inventory entries before filtering by selected ID, and apply the producer’s nonempty-event rule. Keep the explicit ID-zero handling.
findings.requested_evidence: Refuse both malformed positive-posting controls on the persisted and live shapes. Retain the successful pair with an unrelated collector-shaped ID-zero post.
findings.title: Require readable positive postings in source inventories

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The evaluator matches the selected ID, event, frame and posting time to a unique record on the correct source. The passing case rejects 513 for 586, 539 for 622 and a duplicated selected record in both representations.

The original late callback with zero periodic counts now characterizes. A callback predating survivor 586 and counts contradicting later sample timestamps refuse. R3-F1 concerns the separate bounds of target arming and disposal.

The supplied earlier-end, decreasing-count and early-stop regressions pass. The same protected-window defect remains between the last periodic sample and the earliest possible zero-count read. A stop at 22:52:08.3500000Z still characterizes.
An explicit integer ID of zero is skipped as a non-owning failed post. Selection of zero still refuses. Both behaviors passed on the two row shapes. R3-F4 concerns malformed positive postings.
Count accepts integers from zero through Int32.MaxValue. Both affected survivor count fields preserve zero, observed positive, negative and oversized outcomes in the passing regressions.

The live collector constructs its header through NewCallbackLossRow and invokes the same CallbackLossRound7 entry point named by the language-bound identifier. The retained 224949Z row keeps CallbackLossSettled. R3-F5 concerns the separate offline output.
